source.title: Optimization in Machine Learning: a Distribution-Space Approach
source.authors: Yong-Qiang Cai; Qian-Xiao Li; Zuo-Wei Shen

record.file_problem: Full paper text, including appendices, is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper compares its distribution-space optimizer with direct parameter-space training and reports training loss or accuracy for neural networks, including an MNIST CNN. These results bear on initialization sensitivity and optimization outcomes, but do not test the benchmark error claims in the versions directly.
record.gate_note: Rows cover the paper's own direct-training and distribution-space results on MNIST and the reported 1D regression outcomes. References to results from prior work are not rows. Values available only in figures are recorded as figure only; no precise values are inferred from plots.
record.test_reason: The study tests a distribution-space optimizer and initialization sensitivity of final training outcomes. It does not test any listed version: initialization sweeps do not measure V4's training speed, trainable depth, or signal and gradient preservation; the other versions' required comparisons are also absent.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors propose a convex distribution-space relaxation and mixture-based algorithms, illustrating approximation improvements and initialization robustness on simple examples. Practical performance depends on the mixture basis, sampling adds computational overhead, and the regression dimensional reduction need not preserve convexity.
record.recipe_differences: The paper proposes distribution-space optimization over mixture distributions and compares it with conventional parameter-space optimization; it does not reproduce the original methods in the listed sources.
record.method_sensitivity: Direct parameter-space results vary with initialization and learning rates in 1D regression; MNIST results vary with network size, mixture basis and mixture component count. The authors state that distribution-space performance depends on choosing a suitable basis.

fits_no_version.finding: Direct parameter-space training on MNIST is sensitive to initialization scale; distribution-space training is more robust, but its relative performance depends on network size and mixture basis.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In the tested MNIST tasks, distribution-space optimization reduces initialization sensitivity of final training outcomes compared with direct parameter-space optimization.

fits_no_version.finding: For 1D regression, direct SGD outcomes depend on initialization and learning rates; distribution-space outcomes are described as practically independent of initial conditions.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In the tested 1D regression problems, distribution-space optimization is less sensitive to initialization than direct SGD.

record.peer_reviewed: Communication on Applied Mathematics and Computation
record.problems: The experiments are described as simple and are not large-scale benchmark studies. Several reported results are only plotted, and the paper notes that performance depends on the choice of mixture basis. The 1D example includes a dimensional reduction whose resulting mixture-coefficient problem need not remain convex.
record.rows_left_out: No additional reported outcomes on the claim's versions were found. Prior-work results mentioned in the introduction and related work were excluded because they are cited rather than generated by this study.

untested.parts: Near-zero training classification error on CIFAR-10/100, including corrupted labels, and its dependence on model size or training recipe.
Teacher-student ReLU problems, spurious local minima, and extra student neurons.
Depth degradation, identity shortcuts, and the stated initialization-based alternatives.
Activation-matched initialization preserving signals and gradients; faster learning and greater trainable depth; orthogonal versus Gaussian initialization and very deep convolutional training.
Recovery, curvature dynamics and divergence relative to a measured stability threshold. Reported divergence at a large regression learning rate does not establish these.
Training speed and learning-rate tolerance with versus without batch normalization, including Fixup.

record.verdict_notes: All row states are cannot_determine relative to the listed versions because none measures their specified effects. This does not imply the study's reported initialization sensitivity or method comparisons are unreadable.

versions.untested_parts: CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, corrupted or random labels, zero or near-zero training classification error, model size, training duration and early stopping.
Two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems, spurious local minima, and varying student versus teacher width.
Depth comparisons with and without identity shortcuts, plain tanh training with special initialization, and residual training without normalization.
Matched initialization schemes, signal or gradient propagation, depth scaling, orthogonal versus Gaussian weights, and 10,000-layer networks.
Training above a stability limit, loss-curvature dynamics, sharpness behavior and divergence relative to a stability threshold.
Batch normalization versus no normalization for training speed or learning-rate tolerance.

rows.subject: one-hidden-layer neural network with ReLU activations
rows.operation_detail: Direct parameter-space SGD training on the 1D regression task; leaky-ReLU was used to improve training.

conditions.value: 1D regression with 3000 samples uniformly distributed on [-1, 1]

rows.note: The text states this is the best hyperparameter configuration and says direct optimization is sensitive to initialization and learning rates; no exact loss value is stated.
rows.check: The direct-training implementation uses leaky-ReLU. This row records the best selected hyperparameter configuration, not a typical random-initialization outcome. Regression loss does not measure any listed version.

rows.subject: Algorithm 1 distribution-space model
rows.size_stated: n varied; figure uses n as horizontal axis
rows.stage_stated: trained by projected gradient descent over mixture coefficients
rows.operation_detail: Distribution-space optimization on 1D regression using triangular mixture basis.
rows.uncertainty: Monte Carlo fluctuation shown as error bars in Figure 3(a)
rows.note: The figure caption states the distribution-space result is essentially independent of initial condition; its plotted loss values are not given numerically.
rows.check: Performance of the proposed distribution-space method does not measure a listed version. After the product-distribution dimensional reduction, this experiment's coefficient problem need not remain convex.

rows.subject: one-hidden-layer neural network with ReLU activations
rows.operation_detail: Direct parameter-space training with Adam for 30 epochs at learning rate 0.001; first-layer initialization scale swept.
rows.note: The paper reports the sweep and provides plotted results, without exact training metric values in text.
rows.check: The MNIST one-hidden-layer model uses cosine activations, not ReLU. The sweep measures final outcomes after 30 epochs, without testing activation-matched initialization, propagation, training speed or trainable depth.
